newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks open weaker, under selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks open weaker, under selling pressure.

text.p: Tokyo stocks opened weaker on Tuesday, as the market remained under selling pressure after the previous day's sharp tumble. The yen's further weakening against the dollar overnight prompted fears of foreign investors' sales, dragging down the market, brokers said.

AT 0018 GMT, the benchmark Nikkei 225 average was down 65.39 points, or 0.37 percent, at 17,414.95, after briefly slipping to 17,305.25. Its March futures were 10 points higher at 17,470, after dropping sharply.
"The Nikkei 225 will be weaker today, as it does not seem to have hit a bottom yet," said Hiroshi Morimoto, general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
Brokers said they would focus on whether the benchmark stock index remains above the key 17,000 level by the close.
